failures.title: BMW B58D30M0 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Cooling System Leaks - plastic vent lines and oil filter housing (2015-2019)
items.whatHappens: The Gen 1 B58's plastic vent lines and coolant junctions crack under heat cycles, and the oil filter housing warps or fails internally. Coolant loss can be sudden, leading to overheating; the oil filter housing failure can cause catastrophic coolant loss and engine damage. These are the most documented Gen 1 B58 failures.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the vent lines, water pump, and oil filter housing (preventatively) is sufficient. If the engine has overheated due to coolant loss, a full replacement or rebuild is often required - the closed-deck block holds heat and can warp heads.

items.title: PCV System Failure - ruptured diaphragm (2015-2019)
items.whatHappens: The PCV diaphragm in the valve cover is prone to rupture on Gen 1 B58 engines. Symptoms include blue/white smoke from the exhaust, whistling sounds from the engine, and rough idle. If ignored, it can lead to oil consumption and crankcase pressure issues.
items.repairVsReplace: The PCV diaphragm is integrated into the valve cover on later B58 versions, requiring valve cover replacement. On Gen 1 units this is a manageable repair - but if oil starvation has occurred, the engine may be compromised.

items.title: High-Pressure Fuel Pump (HPFP) Failure
items.whatHappens: The high-pressure fuel pump can fail due to manufacturing defects or contaminated fuel. Symptoms include engine misfires, loss of power during acceleration, and difficulty starting.
items.repairVsReplace: HPFP replacement is a standalone repair costing £800-£1,500 - if caught before it causes secondary damage (injector failure, cylinder wash). If injectors have stuck open due to HPFP failure, the engine may need full rebuild.

failures.goodYearsLine: The B58D30M0 is a Gen 1 unit (2015-2019); the B58TU1 (B58B30O1, 2019-2021) introduced a higher-pressure fuel system and split cooling but carried over the same plastic hardware weaknesses. The B58TU2 (2021-present) brought a metal oil pump redesign and 48V mild-hybrid but introduced new complexity.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the B58D30M0
variants.intro: The B58D30M0 is BMW's first-generation B58 engine, produced from 2015 to 2019. It is the 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six that replaced the N55 and features a closed-deck block, twin-scroll turbo, direct injection, and an integrated water-to-air intercooler. Where to find the engine code: - On the engine block - a stamped plate on the left-hand side (viewed from the front) - On the V5C registration document - under engine number - Via a BMW VIN decoder - the 7th and 8th characters of the VIN identify the engine family Commonly confused codes: - B58B30O1 - the TU1 update (2019-2021), with a larger turbo, 350-bar fuel system, and split cooling; higher output (382 hp in some applications) - B58B30M2 - the TU2 update (2021-present), with 48V mild-hybrid, cylinder deactivation, and metal oil pump - B58B30O0 - another Gen 1 variant with slightly different tuning

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement B58D30M0 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used B58D30M0 makes sense for lower-value host vehicles (e.g. higher-mileage F30 340i examples) where a reconditioned unit would exceed the vehicle's value. However, used Gen 1 B58 units carry the same cooling system and PCV risks as the engine being replaced - only buy with documented cooling system history and a compression test. Used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper B58D30M0 recon addresses the Gen 1-specific weak points: new water pump, replacement of all plastic coolant vent lines, oil filter housing refresh, PCV system overhaul, and HPFP inspection. This is the right call for most 40i owners - the engine is fundamentally robust, and addressing the known failure points gives a reliable unit with 12-24 months warranty. Reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full B58D30M0 rebuild is justified for performance applications (track cars, tuned examples) where the closed-deck block and forged internals make it a strong foundation for high-power builds. An upgraded rebuild should include a metal oil pump (retrofit from TU2), upgraded PCV, and forged pistons if pushing beyond 600 hp. Rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All our vetted UK BMW specialists offer supply-only or full supply-and-fit - 12-month warranty on reconditioned units, nationwide delivery available. Supply and fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The B58D30M0 sits in BMW 40i models worth £8,000-£30,000 depending on age and mileage. A reconditioned B58D30M0 at £3,800-£6,000 represents 20-60% of vehicle value - generally viable for most host vehicles. However, for a high-mileage F30 340i worth under £8,000, a used unit (£2,000-£3,800) may be the more financially sensible choice. mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the B58D30M0 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most documented failures are cooling system leaks (plastic vent lines, oil filter housing) and PCV diaphragm rupture. Coolant leaks can lead to sudden overheating and head warping if ignored. PCV failure causes smoking, whistling, and oil consumption. HPFP failures are less common but can damage injectors.

mainEntity.name: Which BMW models have the B58D30M0 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B58D30M0 powered 40i‑badged BMWs from 2015-2019, including the 340i (F30), 440i (F32), M240i (F22), 540i (G30), X3 M40i (G01), X4 M40i (G02), Z4 M40i (G29), and 740i (G11). It is the first‑generation B58, before the TU1 update in 2019. Check your VIN or the engine block stamp to confirm your specific code.

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or reconditioned B58D30M0?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned B58D30M0 is the safer choice because it addresses the Gen 1’s known weak points (cooling system, PCV, HPFP) with a warranty. Used units are cheaper but risk carrying the same unaddressed failures. For high‑mileage cars worth under £8,000, a used engine may be more cost‑effective.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my car has the B58D30M0 and not another B58 variant?

acceptedAnswer.text: The engine code is stamped on the block (left‑hand side) and listed on your V5C or via a BMW VIN decoder. It is commonly confused with B58B30M0, B58B30O1 (TU1), and B58D30M1. Fitting the wrong revision will not work due to different cooling, turbo, and fuel systems.

mainEntity.name: Is the B58D30M0 a reliable engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Overall, the B58 is considered one of BMW’s most robust modern petrol engines, but the Gen 1 D30M0 has specific weak points in the cooling system and PCV. With preventative maintenance (replace coolant hoses, water pump, PCV at 60k-80k miles), it can exceed 150,000 miles. The closed‑deck block and forged internals make it a strong tuner platform.
